newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent tumbles as U.S. markets lose nerve.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent tumbles as U.S. markets lose nerve.

text.p: IPE Brent fell heavily as NYMEX crude and products threw off earlier gains and sank deeply into the red, brokers said.
Feb Brent was trading a hefty 49 cents down at $23.85 by 1717 GMT.
"U.S. products just lost it when they saw that London markets weren't in favour of an upside push and (NYMEX crude) couldn't get above $26.50," said one broker.
"There was a lot of stale length in London and it's being liquidated."
Feb gas oil sank hand in hand with Brent to trade $7.50 a tonne lower at $218.75 shortly before its 1730 close.
Despite forecasts for colder temperatures in the U.S. Northeast and Midwest, NYMEX heating oil did a sharp U-turn from an early rally.
"It completely turned around, the (opening rally) completely failed," a broker said.
Milder European temperatures after a long cold snap also added to the bearish sentiment on gas oil, dealers said.
